title: Motorola's GrapheneOS Phones to Launch in 2027 with Premium Pricing Above Pixel Devices
summary: Motorola and GrapheneOS developers have confirmed that Motorola's first GrapheneOS-supported phones will launch in 2027, priced higher than Google's Pixel lineup. These devices will be premium flagships, likely foldables, due to GrapheneOS's strict hardware requirements for security and privacy features. Only high-end Qualcomm 8-series processors meet these standards, limiting support to expensive models. The installation process will require technical expertise but will be facilitated by a web-based USB installer similar to Pixel devices.
key_points: Motorola's GrapheneOS-supported phones will launch in 2027, marking the first non-Pixel devices to officially support the privacy-focused OS.
The devices will be premium flagships, likely foldables, with pricing expected to exceed Google's Pixel lineup (e.g., above $1,300 for high-end models).
GrapheneOS requires specific hardware security features, currently only met by Google's Tensor chips and Qualcomm's 8-series processors, limiting support to high-end devices.
Motorola's budget phones are unlikely to receive GrapheneOS support due to insufficient update cycles and mid-range chip limitations.
GrapheneOS includes advanced security features such as enhanced memory protection, granular network permissions, customizable app sandboxing, and a duress code for data wiping.
The installation process will require technical expertise but will be supported by a web-based USB installer, similar to the current Pixel setup.
